# The Youngest Billionaires in the World (2026)

Status: DRAFT, Preview only. Not published. Path: /youngest-billionaires/

SEO title: Youngest Billionaires in the World 2026: All 35 Under 30

Meta description: The youngest billionaire is Amelie Voigt Trejes, 20, worth $1.1B on Forbes' 2026 list (as of 1 March 2026). All 35 under-30 billionaires, mapped and ranked.

By Daniel Mercer

_All 35 under-30 billionaires on Forbes' 2026 list, mapped by citizenship and ranked by age. Ages and net worths as of 1 March 2026._

The youngest billionaire in the world is Amelie Voigt Trejes, a 20-year-old Brazilian heir to the WEG industrial machinery fortune, worth $1.1 billion on Forbes' 2026 list (ages and net worths as of 1 March 2026). The youngest self-made billionaires are Mercor's three co-founders, Surya Midha, Brendan Foody and Adarsh Hiremath, each 22 and each worth $2.2 billion on the same date.

I went through every entry in [Forbes' World's Youngest Billionaires 2026](https://www.forbes.com/sites/simonemelvin/2026/03/10/the-worlds-youngest-billionaires-2026/), published 10 March 2026. Forbes counted a record 35 billionaires under 30 as of 1 March 2026, out of 3,428 billionaires in total, according to its [2026 facts and figures](https://www.forbes.com/sites/chasewithorn/2026/03/10/2026-worlds-billionaires-list-facts-and-figures/). Together the 35 held $92.4 billion on that date. I checked each age and net worth against two secondary pages that cite the same Forbes data and found no numeric disagreement. This is a March 2026 snapshot, not a live October 2026 figure, and some people on it may have had birthdays since.

Counted by citizenship, the 35 come from 12 countries as of 1 March 2026. The United States leads with 8, then Germany with 7 and Brazil with 6. Select a country on the map, or use the picker, to see who is behind each number.

## Who is the youngest billionaire in the world?

Amelie Voigt Trejes is the youngest billionaire in the world on Forbes' 2026 list. She was 20 as of 1 March 2026, worth $1.1 billion through a stake of about 2% in WEG, the Brazilian industrial machinery company. She is one of five WEG heirs on the under-30 list, alongside the twins Pedro and Felipe Voigt Trejes and the sisters Livia and Dora Voigt de Assis.

Johannes von Baumbach of Germany was also 20 on 1 March 2026 and is far richer, at $6.6 billion from a stake in drugmaker Boehringer Ingelheim. Forbes calls him the second-youngest, so I keep its order: the source does not publish birth dates, and I could not verify them independently.

One dated caveat. Forbes Brasil's August 2026 survey, priced at 30 June 2026 and [reported by Economic News Brasil on 28 August 2026](https://economicnewsbrasil.com.br/2026/08/28/bilionaria-mais-jovem-do-mundo-amelie-voigt/), put Voigt Trejes at R$6.7 billion and age 21. That is a different reference date and currency, with no US dollar figure published, so I do not mix it into the ranking.

## Who are the top 10 youngest billionaires?

These are the 10 youngest billionaires in the world, by age as of 1 March 2026, with Forbes' net worth on the same date. Ties at the same age keep the order in my dataset, which reverses Forbes' oldest-to-youngest article order.

1. Amelie Voigt Trejes, 20, $1.1B, WEG (Brazil, inherited)
2. Johannes von Baumbach, 20, $6.6B, Boehringer Ingelheim (Germany, inherited)
3. Livia Voigt de Assis, 21, $1.4B, WEG (Brazil, inherited)

6. Surya Midha, 22, $2.2B, Mercor (United States, self-made)
7. Brendan Foody, 22, $2.2B, Mercor (United States, self-made)
8. Adarsh Hiremath, 22, $2.2B, Mercor (United States, self-made)
9. Kevin David Lehmann, 23, $4.9B, dm-drogerie markt (Germany, inherited)

Pedro's twin, Felipe Voigt Trejes, is also 23 and also worth $1.1 billion as of 1 March 2026; he is 11th only because of that tie order. The top 10 held $30.2 billion combined on that date, and only three of them, the Mercor founders, are self-made.

## Who is the youngest self-made billionaire?

The youngest self-made billionaires are Surya Midha, Brendan Foody and Adarsh Hiremath, the co-founders of AI software company Mercor. Each was 22 and worth $2.2 billion as of 1 March 2026. Forbes names Midha the world's youngest self-made billionaire; with no birth dates published, I list the three together.

The other self-made fortunes on the March 2026 list come from the same two places: AI software and prediction markets. Cursor's co-founders Michael Truell and Aman Sanger (both 25), Sualeh Asif and Arvid Lunnemark (both 26) were each worth $1.3 billion. Lovable's Fabian Hedin, 26, had $1.6 billion. Polymarket's Shayne Coplan, 27, had $1.0 billion. Scale AI founder Alexandr Wang, 29, had $3.2 billion, and Kalshi co-founders Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara, both 29, had $1.3 billion each. Forbes calls Lopes Lara the youngest self-made woman billionaire.

I have traced one of these fortunes in depth in my [Michael Truell net worth](https://visionarytalks.com/michael-truell-net-worth/) file. For how I weigh the evidence and limits behind an AI investor's estimated fortune, see my [Daniel Gross net worth](https://visionarytalks.com/daniel-gross-net-worth/) investigation. Startup valuations have moved since March 2026, and I have not re-verified these fortunes against later rounds, so treat them as March figures.

## Are there any Gen Z billionaires?

Yes. Using [Pew Research Center's definition](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2019/01/17/where-millennials-end-and-generation-z-begins/) of Gen Z as anyone born in 1997 or later, at least 29 of the 35 under-30 billionaires are Gen Z. Everyone aged 28 or younger on 1 March 2026 was born after 1 March 1997. The six who were 29 on that date could have been born in 1996 or early 1997, and the sources I opened do not publish birth dates, so I do not count them.

Of those 29 Gen Z billionaires, 9 are self-made as of 1 March 2026: the three Mercor founders, the four Cursor co-founders, Fabian Hedin and Shayne Coplan. The rest inherited. For what typical US household wealth looks like by age, see my guide to [net worth by age](https://visionarytalks.com/net-worth-by-age/).

## Inherited vs self-made

Inheritance still dominates. As of 1 March 2026, 23 of the 35 under-30 billionaires inherited their fortunes and 12 are self-made. The inherited group held $72.2 billion, against $20.2 billion for the self-made group, and its median net worth was $1.9 billion against $1.3 billion.

Age splits the two groups cleanly. Of the 15 people under 25 on 1 March 2026, 12 inherited; the only self-made billionaires that young are the three Mercor founders. Family clusters account for much of the inherited side: five WEG heirs from Brazil, and four members of Germany's von Baumbach family, whose Boehringer Ingelheim stakes came to $26.4 billion between them.

Nationality splits them too. All eight US citizens on the list are self-made as of 1 March 2026, while every under-30 billionaire from Germany, Italy, Ireland, South Korea, France, Norway, China and the UAE is classed as inherited. One borderline case: Abbas Sajwani founded AHS Properties in 2021, but Forbes does not mark him self-made because he is the son of DAMAC founder Hussain Sajwani, so I label him inherited.

## Who is the richest kid in the world?

Forbes' 2026 list has no one under 20, so it cannot name a billionaire child or teenager. The youngest people on it were 20 as of 1 March 2026. The richest of those two 20-year-olds is Johannes von Baumbach, at $6.6 billion. The richest person under 30 is a tie between Clemente Del Vecchio, 21, and Luca Del Vecchio, 24, each worth $6.8 billion on the same date through a stake of about 12.5% in Delfin, the holding company tied to EssilorLuxottica.

## Method

- List date: [Forbes' World's Youngest Billionaires 2026](https://www.forbes.com/sites/simonemelvin/2026/03/10/the-worlds-youngest-billionaires-2026/), published 10 March 2026 and updated 17 March 2026, with net worths as of 1 March 2026. Research checked 16 October 2026.
- Ages are ages at the list date, 1 March 2026, as Forbes reported them. Some people may have had birthdays since.
- Inherited means not marked self-made by Forbes. I follow Forbes' self-made flag and do not reclassify anyone.
- Ties at the same age are ordered as in my dataset, which reverses Forbes' oldest-to-youngest article order. Forbes does not publish birth dates, so I could not verify the order within an age.
- Countries are citizenship, not residence. Net worths are Forbes' US dollar estimates on 1 March 2026; I did not use Bloomberg figures.
- I cross-checked every figure against two secondary pages that republish the Forbes data, ValueAddVC and Visual Capitalist. No numbers disagreed; I use Forbes' spelling of names where Visual Capitalist differs.
